** Σᾰμάρεια** [ᾰρ], ἡ,

4543:
** Σᾰμοθρᾴκη**,
_Ionic dialect_ **Σαμοθρηΐκη**, ἡ, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Samothrace”, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.47}}; the seat of the mysteries of the Cabeiri, {{Refs|[prev. author] 2.51}}; called Σάμος Θρηϊκίη in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.12, “hymnus ad Apollinem” 34}}; and simply Σάμος, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.78, 753}}. _adjective_ **Σᾰμόθρᾳξ** (not Σαμοθρᾴξ),{{Refs 4th c.AD+|Hdn.Gr. 1.42, 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.187}} H., etc.; _Ionic dialect_ _plural_ Σαμοθρήϊκες {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.51, 8.90}}; also **Σᾰμοθρᾴκιος**, _Ionic dialect_ **Σαμοθρηΐκιος**, η, ον, {{Refs|[prev. author] 7.59, 108.}}
4544:
** Σάμος** [ᾰ], ἡ,
“Samos”, the name of several Greek islands:
**1** old name for Κεφαλληνία (which see), {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.634, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.671}}; also called Σάμη,{{Refs|1.246, “hymnus ad Apollinem” 429}}; though this, _accusative_ to others, is a town on the island: hence _adjective_ **Σαμαῖος**, α, ον, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 10.2.13.}}
**2** Σάμος Θρηϊκίη, see at {Σαμοθρᾴκη}.
**3** “Samos”, the large island over against Ephesus, first in {{Refs|“hymnus ad Apollinem” 41}}: hence _adjective_ **Σάμιος**, α, ον, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.70, etc.}}; ἡ Σαμία (i.e. γῆ) {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. passage], 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Lapidibus” 62}}; also Σ. ἀστήρ, clay with medicinal properties, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.178}}:—**Σαμιακός**, ή, όν, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 13. (Acc. to 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 8.3.19, 10.2.17, σάμος}} was an old word signifying **a height.**)

** σαρδόνυξ**, ῠχος, ὁ,
(σάρδιον) **sardonyx**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 216, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 5.46, “Anthologia Graeca” 1.116, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 3.7.5, “BJ” 5.5.7, NT.Rev.21.20, Pseudo-Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fluv.” 20.4, etc.}}The stone was called ὄνυξ when the dark ground was simply spotted or streaked with white, but σαρδόνυξ if the different colours were disposed in layers.

4572:
** σεαυτοῦ**, -ῆς,
also **σαυτοῦ**, -ῆς, _Ionic dialect_ **σεωυτοῦ**, ῆς, reflexive _pronoun_ of _2nd pers._, **of thyself**, etc., in _masculine_ and _feminine_ of _genitive_, _dative_, and _accusative_ _singular_, first in {{Refs 7th c.BC+|7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 87, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 97, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.45, 108}}; ἐν σαυτοῦ (variant{-ῷ}) γενοῦ contain thyself, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 950}}: rarely in _neuter_, φίλον ξύλον, ἔγειρέ μοι σεαυτὸ καὶ γίγνου θρασύ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 693:—the Trag. use the longer form (but not so frequently as the shorter), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 547, “OT” 312, etc.:}} —in _plural_ always separated, ὑμῶν αὐτῶν, etc.: and originally separated in _singular_, as in [{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, who always has σοὶ αὐτῷ, σ᾽ αὐτό; and so τὰ σ᾽ αὐτοῦ, τὰ σ᾽ αὐτῆς for τὰ σά αὐτοῦ, etc., see at {σός} I.3.}}] —The separated forms, σοῦ αὐτοῦ, αὐτοῦ σοῦ, etc., were used in _Attic dialect_, not as reflexive, but as _emphatic_ personal pronouns,{{Refs 5th c.BC+|compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 472b, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 632.}}

or ιος (εος in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Archestratus Epicus “fragment” 4.14)}}, ἡ, **the finest wheaten flour**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 2.42}}, **Acut.(Sp.)**{{NT+5th c.BC+|53, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 412, 5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 63.22, 5th c.BC: Strattis Comicus 2 (who has _genitive_ -ιδος), LXX.Gen.18.6, +others, NT.Rev.18.13, etc.}}; σεμιδάρεως is an error in {{Refs 1st c.AD+|“POxy.” 736.82 (1st c.AD)}}:—hence **σεμῐδᾱλίτης** [ῑ] ἄρτος, ὁ, **bread made of** σεμίδαλις, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 2.42, “PPetr.” 3p.179 (3rd c.BC), 3rd c.BC: Diphilus Siphnius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.115c, 1st c.BC: Trypho Grammaticus [prev. work] 109c, 1st c.AD: Athenaeus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 1.2.2, etc.}}:—also **σεμιδάλιν** (={-ιον}), τό, {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|“PLond.” 2.190.45 (3rd c.AD), “Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”}} (Cf. Assyr. **samīdu**, Aramaic _semīdā_ in same sense.)

4594:
** σήμερον**,
_adverb_ **to-day**, {{NT+8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.30, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.186, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 683, “PHib.” 1.65.13 (3rd c.BC), “SIG” 1181.11 (Rhenea, 2nd c.BC), NT.Matt.27.19, etc.}}; _Doric dialect_ **σάμερον** [ᾱ] {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.28, “P.” 4.1}}; _Attic dialect_ **τήμερον** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 123, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 68, etc., cf. Moer. p.364 P. (though σήμερον}} is sometimes found in Comedy texts, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 80, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 121)}}; εἰς τ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174a; τὸ τ. [prev. work] 176e}}; τὸ τ. εἶναι **to-day**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Cra.” 396e; ἡ τ. ἡμέρα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.40}}; also in the form **τήμερα** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 401 (assuming variant), compare 296}}. (Prob. from κ**y**ᾱμερον, containing stem **[kcirc]yo-** 'this', cf. Lithuanian _šis_ 'this', Latin _ci-tra_: σήμερον (τήμερον) is to ἡμέρα as σῆτες (τῆτες) to ἔτος.)
